prize_parts.citation: for empirical evidence on how trade exposure and technological change reshape local labour markets, employment and wages

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. In round 1 I preferred B034 (Melitz and Helpman) and named B036 as the strongest alternative, with the condition that I would credit Autor, Dorn and Hanson if I moved to it. I now move to B036 for reasons that are about the work, not about how many colleagues prefer it. First, the China-shock programme answers a first-order question, who bears the adjustment costs of trade, with designs that are transparent enough to be attacked, and they have been attacked for about a decade. The central finding of concentrated, persistent local adjustment costs has survived in qualified form, and later work has refined the magnitudes without reversing the sign. That is the kind of replication record I look for before recognising empirical work. It is also close to my own method, where real data is used to test theory and the contribution is measured by what survives scrutiny. Second, credit is now defined more precisely than I thought in round 1. My opening Autor-Katz pairing split the technology and trade strands and fully credited neither. The programme that gives the entry its causal weight is jointly authored by Autor, Dorn and Hanson. Third, the point that moved me most is that the B034 priority question, which I called my most serious reservation, cannot be settled on the evidence available to me. I weigh a cleanly credited, well-tested discovery above one whose attribution I cannot defend. My citation is anchored on exposure and adjustment, and it avoids claiming a size or a long-run elasticity.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still the one I raised in round 1. The long-run size and persistence of the effects, and the shift-share exposure instruments, remain debated, so the Committee could be recognising a robust qualitative finding rather than a settled quantitative one. The entry also bundles two strands. A trade-centred trio leaves Katz and the task and skill-bias lineage uncredited, and part of that lineage belongs to Acemoglu (recognised in 2024) and to Levy and Murnane outside the credited set. The thematic overlap with the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes is real. I also cannot judge the full set of critiques of the exposure measures from the supplied evidence. Finally, B034 remains the cleaner two-person credit and the older, more fully mature contribution. If the Committee finds the persistence debate unsettled, that case is stronger than my current ordering implies.

responses.point: Fredriksson rejected my Autor-Katz pairing, arguing that the task framework has the most diffuse attribution on the ballot and that dropping Dorn and Hanson would strip the citation of the evidence with the largest policy effect.
responses.response: I accept this. My opening treated the task framework as the core, and that is the hardest strand to attribute cleanly, since credit is shared with an earlier laureate and with authors outside the entry. I now credit the strand with the sharpest attribution and the longest critical record. I agree that the citation should state its scope openly, so that it is not read as a ruling on who originated the task framework.

responses.point: Dreber argued that the Acemoglu overlap points toward the China-shock core, not away from it, and that the shift-share debate should be handled through careful citation wording.
responses.response: I agree. The overlap concern I raised in round 1 is a reason to avoid building the citation on the theory of tasks, and it does not support the Autor-Katz pair. I also accept the point on the debate over exposure measures. A result that has been challenged and still holds in qualified form is evidence of maturity. I would keep the wording to the evidence on exposure and labour-market adjustment and leave out any stated effect size.

responses.point: Enflo separated Melitz's selection mechanism from Krugman's 2008 prize and treated Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as largely empirical or quantitative precursors rather than competing claims to the model.
responses.response: I still agree that selection and reallocation across firms are a distinct mechanism, and I would defend B034 as a prize-worthy discovery. Our difference is how much unresolved priority weighs. Bernard and Jensen documented the exporter facts before Melitz, and Eaton and Kortum are a related but separate line. I credit Melitz with the integration, but I cannot show from the supplied evidence that a two-name citation would withstand the priority challenge. That uncertainty about attribution, not any doubt about the idea, is why B034 is now my first alternative. If colleagues can supply a precise, defensible statement of priority, I would reconsider.

responses.point: Friberg answered my priority question on B020 by narrowing the citation to demand estimation with endogenous prices, defending the Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes core, and rejecting the idea that the 2021 prize sets a preferred method.
responses.response: That is a fair answer and I take it seriously. I was not arguing that design-based methods should be the standard. Structural demand estimation answers counterfactual questions that reduced-form designs cannot, and I accept the complementarity. The narrower citation does address the Bresnahan and Reiss priority concern. What stays open for me is that the trio's credit is a choice between the demand-estimation strand and the dynamic-games strand, and credit for the method is shared among more people than a three-name cap allows. I keep B020 as an alternative on its merits, but I judge B036 to have the tighter attribution.

responses.point: Teorell now prefers Autor, Dorn and Hanson, and he argued that a citation should credit the evidence on local labour-market adjustment rather than a particular elasticity, and that the exposure-measure critiques should be reviewed before the Committee finalises.
responses.response: I agree with the wording principle and my citation follows it. I also support his suggestion that the Committee review the shift-share critiques and the persistence evidence before the vote. A specific finding that would change my view is evidence that the headline local employment and wage effects fail under the most credible alternative exposure measures. I know of no such finding, but I cannot rule it out from the evidence supplied.

uncertainties: Whether the long-run persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects, and the shift-share exposure instruments, hold up well enough for the Committee to treat this as a settled discovery rather than a contested estimate.

Whether leaving out Katz and the task and skill-bias lineage (including Acemoglu, recognised in 2024, and Levy and Murnane) is an acceptable attribution cost, or whether a broader technology-and-labour prize would be more defensible.
How much room the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes leave for another award on the labour-market effects of trade and technology.

Whether the priority questions around B034 (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Yeaple) could be answered well enough that its cleaner two-person credit and greater maturity should win out over my current choice.

My assessment draws on my own reading of the literature and the supplied round-1 files. I have not independently verified any credit attribution, and my corporate-finance background gives me less direct expertise in labour and trade than in contracting and private equity.
statement.conflict_note: Updated for round 2: none apparent from the supplied profile with Autor, Dorn, Hanson or Katz, with Helpman, Melitz or Redding (B034), or with Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn (B020). My adjunct post at Chicago Booth and my co-authorships (Kaplan, Axelson, Weisbach and others) do not connect to the credited names. My field is corporate finance, and B012 is the only neighbouring candidate, which I do not propose. I disclose my long committee overlap with Hassler (the chair), Krusell (the secretary), Ellingsen and Svensson as a collegial tie, not a tie to any candidate. I moved from B034 to B036 after the exchange. Conflicts are disclosed here, not adjudicated.
